title: Solid habit tracker with nice features and some room for improvement
body:
I have looked through most habit trackers on the app store, and so far this seems like the one I will likely settle on long-term.  The interface is attractive and the “cards” for building your own HUD for each habit is a nice touch.  I also appreciate the daily overview of all habits and the Apple Watch companion app.  

I cannot quite give it 5 stars though for a few misc. reasons.  One, although it has a quite good Watch app from my testing so far, the lack of more comprehensive complication options is a hindrance.  (Devs, please add complications that work with Infograph Modular in particular!  This is huge for me!)

As well, the GUI, while pretty and generally responsive, suffers a bit from having unusually fiddly buttons.  Either they are too small or the touch sensitivity for them is too low, because I find myself having to press them repeatedly at times to get a response.  I also feel that the New Cards and New Task guis could be streamlined a bit, or at least made more tap-friendly.  They feel a bit awkward to move through quickly, mostly for the same reason of fiddly unresponsive buttons.

As well, I find the swiping behaviour on the main task face a bit unresponsive as well.  It is heavily biased towards up-down swipes and I have to try multiple times to get left/right swiping between tasks to work properly.  Better swipe direction detection would help a lot.

I think my only other minor complaint is that it would be nice if Task screens were a bit more customizable.  The photos are nice, but having the task title all the way at screen bottom and with no text-background option means some photos are hard to read against, or that usable screen real estate goes largely unused (having the option to pin a card there would be nice for instance).  I also somewhat miss the ability to use glyphs for tasks that I have seen in some other habit trackers.

Beyond these quibbles/rough edges, I appreciate the app’s commitment to privacy, on-device data, its’ reasonable pricing, and its’ interesting mix of variable simplicity and customizability.  I have not so far run into any noticeable bugs beyond the minor UI frustrations.  I would love to see more extensive Card options per task, and more Health metric integration, and some Widgets.  Possibly more chart and graph options would also be nice, but I think the current ones do a respectable job, that said.

In summary, I think this is a solid app for the price that provides an enjoyable experience grounded in an appealing design.

Another favourite feature is the ability to add the “journal/notes” and “photo gallery” cards, used to inspire me later on when I need to remember how to meet that goal! 

One last thing: I am so stoked I can access this tool, support your work at a fair and upfront cost, without signing up for a subscription! Thanks again, I do strongly recommend this app.

title: Beautiful Goal-tracker
body:
I love this app! It’s exactly what I was looking for, and the one time premium is totally worth the $$. I don’t understand why so many of these apps are subscription based, so it’s nice to find an app that covers all the features without the ongoing price tag. The interface is smooth and attractive. It’s very simple to use. And yet there are also some nice in depth features if you want to go detailed. There is a convenient streak calendar, separate for each goal. You can keep a journal, track steps and other iOS Health stats, and even create your own custom milestones (such as reaching a certain weight, finishing a study list, or reading a certain number of books). I highly recommend.

My only suggestion is that I would like to be able to colour code or create categories in the overview section.

title: Watch app not working properly
body:
I love tracking my habits, it’s very helpful for me to see how much I’ve accomplished and having that moment to acknowledge for myself that I completed a task is highly rewarding. The iphone app is great with a lovely interface; choosing your own inspiring photo as backgrounds is great! However, I already had that app and didn’t need another.

 I bought this app for the watch incorporation; to be able to check in on the go and track easily from my wrist. But when I check into my watch it will still have the previous days check-in on there, and when it finally syncs up and I am able to check in from the watch, that information is not transferred to my phone. I think it’s working, and when I check my phone, sometimes the same day, sometimes 2 days later it’s unchecked and I have to fill it in from my phone. I would like to not have to open my phone to make sure I have the check-in. It defeats the purpose of why I got it. Please fix this problem, and it will be 5 stars in my books!

title: Beautiful but...
body:
First off, this is hands down one of the best habit tracking apps EVER- I've tried just about all of them but none seem to work for me.

This is one is *nearly* perfect. It's clean, beautiful and easy to use. Especially since it's a habit tracker, the UI can't be messy, ugly or cluttered because that doesn't motivate you to use the app. 

The only other app that I could compare to this one is Productive. Although that app's UI is a bit messy and not very clean,  they give you 5 free habits to track! That's the reason why I took off a star.

If you could add just 2 more free habits (to have a total of 5) I would delete Productive for sure, because then Today would be so much better.

As of now, I guess I'll just keep them both ugh, I really hope the developers read this and take it to consideration.

title: What I needed
body:
I love this app. It pushes me to be consistent. I have 8 or 9 habits that I'm juggling, and although some I can't complete, the ones I do complete like daily push-ups, cold showers, and runs every few days make me feel like a changed person. I have a few minor problems with the app, for example, the fluidity of the switching between habits could be smoother as I can only seem to swipe left or right once I've scrolled all the way to the very top of the habit page, but for the most part, the app runs great. I hope to see an update where more cards, covers, and features in general are introduced, but for the most part, the app is already really great. All in all, I give Today an A, but it still has room to improve on before I can give it an A+. I think that an A+ is possible with the current direction, ideas, and feel, so what it needs to work on is simply more features and polish. Keep it up. 

Thanks.

title: app很好，可是我穷
body: app很好，操作简单，非常适合我这种懒人。为什么给4分，主要是因为我穷。老实说，我只用了打卡功能，但是只能添加3个打卡项目，想要添加更多，需要交30块钱获取完整版。are u kidding me？？如果我爸是马云，我分分钟下单。可惜不是。我犹豫了一天零22个小时，考虑到底要不要卸载。很好的一个app，难道要在这个选项上卡人么？开发者是不是想聚集一群富豪开party？说实话，真的觉得这个app和外面的妖艳j货不一样，是app届的一股清流。希望开发者考虑一下这个门槛儿，10块钱以内我都能接受。开发app难道不是为了能让更多的人用么？如果在这个问题上设这么高门槛儿，那像我这种普通人，分分钟就旋转跳跃闭着眼转身离开了。写这么多，希望开发者能看见并考虑一下，真心喜欢你们的app，可我也是真的穷。祝越来越好。

title: Great but could use an overview of all habit check-ins
body:
I really enjoy the app. Its fairly easy to check-in, it looks great and offers variability in the habit setting (for example weekly habits or multiple check-ins in a day).
That said, i would love to see a feature that shows all of my habits at once - like a monthly view or a list with all my check-ins.
I would also like if it showed a green checkmark for the daily habits when completed (now it’s only after finishing the weekly plan for the daily habits - that doesn’t really make sense to me). Thank you for this app and keep up the good work!

title: By far the best habit tracking app!
body:
Guys this is the best habit/goal tracking app on the market. Believe me I tried every single one.

For each habit you can create cards like milestones, charts, counters and notes. You can add the milestone card many times and change the header to rewards, to buy or anything else. Note taking or journaling is also very good for diet/fitness tracking or expense tracking habits.

Why do you stop improving this app? It was over one year since the last update. I will be very happy to see web/iPad version and printing functions for notes or the whole dashboard.

This app is worth every penny you pay.
Please keep up good work!

Cheers

title: Gute App mit viel Potential
body:
Mir gefällt die App sehr gut, aber noch besser fände ich es, wenn man eine Gewohnheit beliebig mit Tages- und Uhrzeiten versehen kann.

Ein einfaches Beispiel: 
Ich meditiere unter der Woche um 7:00 Uhr, am We soll es aber erst um 9:00 Uhr sein. Es ist zwar möglich zwei Zeiten anzugeben, dann werde ich allerdings auch um 7:00 Uhr erinnert...Natürlich könnte ich dafür jeweils eine neue Gewohnheit erstellen, aber das wird schnell sehr viel und ich denke, dass man das mit komplett voneinander unabhängigen Tagesprogrammen fixen kann, man müsste nur bei den Tagen individuelle Uhrzeiten vergeben können statt einer oder mehrer fixer Zeiten. 😉

Jedenfalls stelle ich mir das so vor. Was meinst das Team dazu? Geht das? 

Wenn ja, gibt es von mir definitiv 5 Sterne!
😃

title: Horrible last Update
body:
The last update has significantly worsen all workflows for me. 
Now I can’t see in the today habit tablewview overview which habits I have already accomplished today. Instead of a  check mark there is only a number. There is no way to check ‘which habits have I not fulfilled today yet’. In fact it seem like the Today tab and the All tab carry the exact same information (???)
In the calendar view it’s not possible to check a day with force touch anymore. That was such an important feature. This feature was replaced by the far less more important ‚skip feature‘ which is totally non sense for me. You could have placed the skip feature more locally. For example in the habit main Screen it self. 
I don’t like the new pop up for adding check in’s either. It takes now 3 clicks instead of one to check in for an old day... you could have let force touch for one day and normal tap for the multiple check in pop up. 
It happens often that I forget to check in for one day and have to check in for the day before. So the whole process takes up significantly more time. I’m pretty sure that’s the case for most people too. 

Please come back to the old quality UX workflows or something that is just as easy and I will update to 5 stars. Guys I have been a big fan but this update is a huge step back for me

UPDATE:
Dev Team reacted quite quick - the last update has significantly improved the check in experience once again. Happy to have single tap check in back. I like the solution with the small +\- pop up. Much better than the big screen solution. 

Thank you for the last update. 
Changed my rating to 5 stars ;-)

PS: one last issue remaining:
In the Habit tableView (burger Menu)
When you swipe a cell from right to left (check in) you can only see a number in the circle becoming +1. I believe earlier it changed in a way to mark that you have checked in that habit today. I understand this has been changed to make room for multiple check in per days, but still some kind of marker would be nice. This way you just don’t know which habits you have checked in at least once today. ( with the Green checkmark you were able to quickly check what habits you still have left todo)

title: Peut encore progresser
body:

Par exemple, ce serait bien i un fil d’actualité qui nous explique comment prendre de bonne habitude ou comment font les gens qui réussissent à les prendre. De plus dans la description on nous parle de perdre ses mauvaises habitudes : il nous faut des explications. En quoi cette application s’intéressent à nos mauvaises habitudes? 

Par ailleurs, ils y’a des bugs. Quand je clique sur mon profil, l’application plante

Il faudrait également pouvoir mettre plus de carte. Les cartes proposer sont bien mais vraiment trop peu nombreuses.

Nous donner des exemples de bonnes habitudes avec les cartes à utiliser.

Le widget par contre est vraiment génial pour tout avoir à l’œil. On peut même checker une habitude directement dans le widget. Pas besoin d'ouvrir l’appli !

Gros problème avec les complication AppleWatch j’ai l’impression quelle ne son pas compatible avec WatchOS 5 (en tout cas elle ne s’affiche pas avec mes cadran).

Ce serait bien de nous laisser le choix des complications en en ajoutant plus !

L’application Apple Watch est très bien par contre.

J’espère vraiment que cette appli sera amener à s’améliorer. Elle peut être d’une aide bienvenue !

title: Great app but could be better
body:
This app is exactly what I needed. I love the look of it. I use it every day. 

My only complaints are these: 

-I would love to be able to add notes and customize the reminders. Maybe to put details about how to do the habit, maybe a motivational quote... Hopefully I’m understandable.

-An easier, quicker way to UN-check an habit, check-in by check-in. Maybe with an upwards swipe. But at least I think it should be doable directly in the « list » tab of the habits.

-I also believe an habit tracker app should have the capacity to put in certain objectives for any habit. For example, a number of pages to read for a daily reading habit. Or a certain quantity of water to drink each day. Anyways it would be great to put in the units ourselves and not be restrained to certain units. Also a great idea would be to be able to deconstruct habits in multiple steps based on these objectives. For example, each check-in would mean I read 10 pages out of the 50. 

I hope I made sense. Thank you.

Good looks,

Tom Paupe

title: Recommendations to achieve 5 stars
body:
In my opinion this is a truly wonderful app. It has a one off payment that is much cheaper than any other apps like it with memberships, and it gives you a great amount of features.

Here are a few recommendations to turn this 4-star rating into a solid 5:
1) The ability to pause habits needs to be added, as people can’t do all their habits if they are travelling/on a holiday, etc.
2) A cool little feature you could add is being able to change when a new day starts. This is very helpful for people who stay up late, because it means I can tick habits off even if it is past 12:00am.
3) A big feature that has to be added is being able to track bad habits. E.g. if someone has a smoking habit they can track how many times they smoke a day, and the less the better.
4) I noticed a small error in text. If I allow multiple checkins per day on a habit and then select ‘1 time’, it says on the habit screen ‘1 times per day’ instead of ‘1 time per day’. Just a little grammatical error I thought I’d make the developers aware of.

I really hope the developers see this review, and if you do, I want to thank you for this amazing app. For its price I think it surpasses other apps in this field, such as Productivity or Streaks. I know you are all working very hard to perfect this app, but please address the issues I have presented above, as it would make me and countless other users ecstatic.

Edit: Thanks for responding. I can’t wait to see the big updates in the future. I just want to address one more issue with the UI of this app. It would be much more motivating if you could see your streak without the need to swipe up. It would be neat if you could also see the streak of each habit on the page where you can see all your habits, instead of just seeing the number of checkins for the day. Thank you once again for reading reviews and responding. I’ll be sure to change my rating to 5 stars when the updates come out!

title: Beautiful and motivating
body:
I love this app. It's incredibly customisable, and looks gorgeous. 

I'm a very visual person, so the combination of large pictures and colourful calendars/graphs is great. I really feel motivated to tick things off, more than any other habit app. 

Apart from the couple of things I'd like to see (that I'll mentioned next), I really can't fault this app. It's amazing. 

As for suggestions:

Edit: This has been included!
• Some way of recording habits that you do more than once a day (e.g. brushing teeth morning and night). At the moment I'm just creating two habits, but it'd be nice to be able to condense it into one. 

• Speaking of condensing: Categories (e.g. Health, Skills, etc.). This would be useful if you've got lots of habits for different areas of life (like me), and want to briefly view one 'area'. 

Edit: This has been included!
• Multiple notifications per day. For example, if you're wanting to drink water throughout the day, or do a habit both day and night.

title: The habits app I’d been waiting for
body:
Combines reminders with recording and allows you to view ‘lead indicators’ like calories consumed beside ‘lag indicators’ like your weight. 

It integrates with Apple Health so no double entry - either input here when reminded, or use data collected by your phone or watch. You can set up cards to monitor just about anything. 

Many apps claim to be clean, powerful, flexible and beautiful. This one actually is!

The free version allows you all the access you need to see if it meets your needs, if it does the price is eminently reasonable. 

Lots more good stuff in the pipeline too. 

Only tiny quibble is that the intro video goes a bit too fast for me. Overall nigh-on indispensable for me.

body:
I scoured the appstore for habit apps, wanting to see if an app would help with achieving done goals. I eventually downloaded about 12 to try - note that some apps don't let you try it out without forking out at all so the in-app upgrade was a good option allowing me to see the apps potential (the only alternative being releasing a free demo version separately).

As I tried them all out I kept coming back to this one, eventually narrowing it down to 5 apps with the functionality that suited me. I can't believe some apps out there have a yearly subscription circa £30, though I would have considered it if it did everything I wanted (but they didn't!). I am pleased to support good development and invest in apps that make a difference in my life, and this one is a steal at £5 as far as I'm concerned. 

If others are looking for an app to build new or persevere with existing habits, I can't recommend this enough. If you need one that allows you to track bad habits in order to give something up then this app doesn't really facilitate that at the time of writing this review, although that wasn't a requirement for me. 

Being a very visual person (like other reviewers here), flicking through the cards with images I've chosen for myself to 'advertise' my goal is really motivating and almost introduces a type of gamification to the whole process. It's immediately one of my most frequently opened apps and makes me do a task to get it ticked off, which is just the effect I was after.

I look forward to seeing where the developers take this app. They've been quick to respond to my suggestions and feedback so I'm keen to see what they do in the reporting side, which is a small weakness now (I only stumbled on the charts in the profile section by accident!) It'd be great to have charts to show cumulative effort and consistency, and compare progress of habits in the same view. I would also enjoy a dashboard view like the excellent notification widget shows. However the essence of the app is in the uncluttered separate screen per habit construction which really makes this app. Simple but so powerful. 

Well done neybox!

title: Great app!
body:
I rarely write reviews but the negative ones here annoyed me - yes, it's a paid app with a free trial. Would you pay £4 for an app without testing it first? 
How is that a surprise when it says so on the main page of the app? Good software cannot be free.

The app is very well designed. It does what I wanted it to - helps me keep track of habits I want to develop. The addition of cards which let you create little motivation boards was what made me pay for the full version. 

I didn't realize I wanted the motivation boards but they made all the difference - let's say you want to run in the mornings. You've barely got enough motivation to sit up and grab your phone. Leaving your bed seems impossible. You launch the app, see the cover of your running habit, scroll down and look through pictures of how you'll look like if you stick with the habit, the data on how long you've been running, your weight graph. Now you want to go running.

title: 一番のお気に入り
body:
長年使っていますが、iPhoneの中で一番お気に入りのアプリです。
デザインがとても洗練されていて、操作もスマート。習慣管理だけでなく、健康記録や日記など色々な用途に応用できる柔軟さがあります。
私は毎日使っていて、生活の一部になっています。
サポートもとても丁寧で頼できるアプリです。

As someone who worked in broadcast graphics design and even received the Good Design Award in Japan, I can say that Today is one of the most thoughtfully designed apps I have used.
Good design is not just about beauty. It must communicate clearly, be intuitive to use, and go beyond the user's expectations. Today achieves this balance remarkably well.
Its interface is elegant, flexible, and incredibly practical. I use it every day for habits, health tracking, and journaling.
In my opinion, it is one of the most refined and well-designed apps available on the iPhone.

title: コンセプトとデザインは素敵。サポートは最悪。
body:
コンセプト的にはいたってシンプルなアプリです。初期設定の壁紙はセンスが良くて、やる気が出ます。

ただ、Dropboxとの同期機能があるものの、iPhoneを買い換えるなどアプリの再インストールを行った場合、データが消えてしまう事があります。サポートに尋ねたところ、まず返事をいただくまで3週間がかかり、ついに回答が来たら1行だけの単純内容で「現在、インポートはできません。」と、何の解決にもならない残念な内容でした。

デザイン的には使い方がよく、かつ見やすいから、まだ使い続けたいと思いますが、そのサポート体制とインポート機能の不十分さには閉口します。くれぐれもご注意を。

title: 自分好みのカスタマイズ
body:
目標に対してのカード(自分が表示したい数字、写真の情報の塊)による習慣管理が斬新。新しいカード追加予定ということで期待‼︎

これらが追加希望になれば嬉しく思います。かなり欲張りですが笑

◆チェックインの簡略化
壁紙の画面で習慣をチェックインする時に右上のチェックインボタンを押して進行状況の画面まで行き、＋ボタンを押すのが面倒。壁紙画面で下スワイプをしたら即チェックインできたらと思います。
同様に、すべての習慣一覧で下スワイプで一括チェックインできたら便利。

◆一つの習慣カレンダーに対しての子カレンダー追加
筋トレの習慣を例に挙げると、スクワット100回、腹筋100回、背筋100回、、のように全ての習慣表示一覧が筋肉で埋め尽くされちゃいます…
子カレンダーを全て達成すると親カレンダーをチェックインするようにして欲しい。また、逆も然り。
もしくは、アウトライン表示で子カレンダーを畳めるようにして欲しい。

◆カスタムチャートの数値、平均棒グラフだけでなく合計の折れ線グラフ
習慣の総合計時間を計ることで、モチベーションに繋げる為。

◆1日の開始終了時間を変更
寝る時間が遅いので、習慣のチェックインが飛んでしまうことがある為。

◆フォントカラー、フォントサイズの変更
白背景の壁紙を使うと読めなくなる。また、20文字以上入力すると、壁紙の画面では…で読めなくなる為。

◆フォトギャラリーの写真に、撮影データから撮影日時を読み取って表示するオプション
写真で変化を記録する際に日付がないことで履歴を追いづらい為。

◆フォトギャラリーのアップロード写真数をカウントするカード
何枚追加したかわかりづらい為。追加した枚数でモチベーション維持に繋げる為。

◆初回起動時にタスク一覧表を選択するオプション
壁紙画面から始まるので、いちいち習慣一覧に戻ってからチェックインするのが面倒くさい為。

◆グラフ数字をExcel、テキストデータへの出力
他データへ加工したい為。

◆マイルストーンの自動生成
習慣が目標通りチェックインされた段階で(例えば週5/5回)、入力したマイルストーンが全て復活する設定が出来ると良い。再入力が面倒くさい為、現状使っていない。

◆カスタムチャートの色変更
全て青色のグラフで表示されるので、複数の数字管理をするとわかりづらいです。

◆トップへ戻る機能
カードを増やしすぎると、スクロールして上に戻るのが面倒くさいので、上に戻るボタンを搭載したカードを追加して欲しいです。

◆プライバシー機能の強化
指紋認証画面へ入る手前に一瞬、設定している習慣を見ることができる？気のせい？

◆日記
見出しだけでなく、文章の2行目も表示できる設定が欲しいです。

◆サウンドエフェクト
バッジを取得した時にテンションが上がる音を流して欲しいです。runtastic的な。

◆習慣に色付け
全ての習慣を表示している時に運動系、生活習慣系、自己啓発系などカラーで管理できたらと思います。DayOne的な。

◆無期限のタスク
ランダムな日にちで特定の時間にリマインダーを表示して欲しい。

◆プロフィール
プロフィール画面のプロフィールってどうせなら名前を設定できるようにして欲しい。

ワガママですか、アップデートに期待しています！

title: Great tool for those with ADHD
body:
The Today Habit Tracker app has been monumental for me as someone with severe ADHD. Being able to plan ahead and create daily and weekly routines, along with corresponding widgets, has made scheduling and planning daily life a breeze. The app is simple, elegant, and full of features. I have subscribed to a year of premium due to its benefits. However, I’ve noticed it lacks some critical functionality and contains a couple bugs. I’d love to see an update with some or all of the following addressed!
* When selecting “view/edit data” on a custom chart, the app crashes — there is no way to change, remove, or edit the number entered originally.
* Some health categories I am interested in displaying are missing — like medications taken/skipped
* Being able to launch shortcuts or apps within a habit could be a great feature to make completing tasks simpler. * I would love to be able to create a section for “bad habits” — most of what I use the app for is daily and weekly tasks like laundry, meds, and exercise. Having a section for bad habits, like arguing, vaping, drinking, etc. where I could keep track of these habits and focus on quitting them could be great.
* I would also love to see more integration with other third party apps, like Spotify (for quick launching playlists and choosing tunes for each habit), Calm/Headspace (for quickly starting a random or preselected meditation), Nike Run Club (for starting workouts quickly and seeing more detailed information), and possibly smart home apps — like HomeKit, Alexa, LG Thinq, or Tuya — setting routines from within the app and having access to information like washer/dryer time remaining would be monumental.
* The Pillow sleep tracking app, which is made by the same developer, isn’t integrated at all into this app — with sleeping habits being integral to a healthy lifestyle, I’d love to see more feature tie ins between the two.
* Milestones, which are essentially mini checklist widgets sitting below a habit, don’t automatically reset daily with no option to have the app do so. I use this feature for tasks such as my meditation routine, morning rituals, and logging medication I have taken on a specific day. Being able to choose to have these lists reset daily, as well as being able to see a history of what was checked off on what day and when, would go a long way for me.
* The Welzen meditation app, which is prominently featured on a widget, isn’t available in the U.S. app store — once the widget is added, it is functionally useless. I’d love to see a revamped mindfulness feature!
Overall, this app is a great tool for those who need it, and with some improvement, would be an instant purchase for me! As these bugs and missing features are addressed, I will definitely up my rating to 5 stars — this app is very close to being perfect!

title: Beautiful but missing one thing
body:
I’ve been using this app for years. It’s got an absolutely stunning, simple UI design. I continue to use it because of its design, but also the simplicity of just checking off a habit with a tap. No frills, no fuss—no need to sit through way-too-long animations and stories and celebrations every time you do something. It does the job: helping me form habits in a visually appealing way. This app has helped me with journaling, working out, eating better, learning a language, and even walking more.

That said, there are a few things I’m surprised haven’t been implemented yet. The ability to archive or hide habits (when you don’t want to lose your data/history but don’t want to keep tracking it anymore) is the biggest thing that I feel is missing. It can be a bit buggy sometimes as well. Hope improvements keep coming!

title: Nifty App!
body:
As long as you keep your phone with you, you will never forget an important task again. With the app you can set daily or weekly reminders that will notify you to do any chore at anytime of the day, and if you need to complete a task several times a day you can set it up to remind you multiple times a day. The app has beautiful backgrounds and a lovely font. Among other things, I use the app to make sure I drink enough water and stretch at particular times during the day, and water my plants when they need to be watered, since my memory isn’t what it used to be. The app is easy to use! And there is an easy to understand video tutorial that comes with it. Apparently, there are other things the app can do, but I haven’t gotten around to exploring them yet. Use the basic version for free or pay a small fee once for the upgrade. The app will back up your data in case you need to reinstall it, but this feature is probably only available with the upgrade. It was recommended by a teacher, and I am glad I tried it. Now it’s an essential part of my life.

Edit:
Although I enjoy the app, I learned that it breaks often and needs to be reinstalled frequently to get the reminders working again. I still use it to log events, but became tired of reinstalling it and resetting up the reminders, so they haven’t worked for at least a year.

title: What Habit Will You Start Today?
body:
If you want to create a new habit, there is no shortage of apps on the App Store to help you reach your goal. Today eschews the typical list-of-habits interface and instead shows each goal or habit on its own screen, complete with gorgeous background. Swipe left and right between goals, double-tap to check in.

Also atypical in an app of this type is the ability to add additional data. Swipe up to review cards of different types that you have attached to the goal: charts, counters, photos, milestones, notes — anything that might help propel you toward your desired outcome. You can even include Apple Health metrics. (It would be nice, though, if adding weight data in another app would immediately register a check-in.)

Today supports multiple reminders per habit (an important feature for me) and its notifications are rich and actionable. It's Today screen widget makes it easy to update your progress without getting into the app. And I like that you can set daily, weekly, or monthly goals; that specific days can be set for daily goals; and that daily habits can have multiple completions per day.

Another neat feature (if you're into that kind of thing) is that Today awards badges for total completions and streaks. And tucked away in a dark corner are stats for things like habit persistence and what day is the best for getting things done. My only disappointment with the app is its inability to properly track bad habits. If I were tracking (as I am now) whether or not I've had *any* soda, a single check-in could indicate success in abstaining for the day. But if I only want to *limit* my intake to, say, two sodas a day, I can't both log each drink and show success for not going over the limit. Still, the app is fairly new and appears to be supported, and it's well worth the small price for the premium features. I am looking forward to seeing what new features and cards the developer dreams up and maybe this shortcoming will be addressed.

body:

-Just the right amount of customization (not overwhelming and not time consuming).

-Notifications have a unique and pleasant sound (minor, but important to me).

-Badge reward system (might seem silly, but  I find it motivating).

Cons:

Suggestions to the Dev. Team:

-From the main menu, allow the user to simply click on the circle next to each habit as oppose to swiping it for completion.

title: Downloaded March 2019 (EDIT: April 2019)
body:
This app is literally my new best friend! I've always been a motivated person to work on goals and daily habits and this is going to be with me through it all! 

Super sleek, super simple! The cover phots to choose have been perfect for every habit so far; the badges have streaks and check-ins all the way up to a year; setting up each habit personally is super easy and gives lots of options; its connecting with multiple outsiders to track choosen bars; & multiple check ins are great!

There's a few things i would add to it just for the fun of it: 
1. Link with the "Screen Time" on iPhones like the way it does with Apple Health. This would be great because of one of the habits I'm working on is cutting back social media- it can transfer the information here on one of the graphs
2. Allow the photogallery card to change the order of the photos so that was i don't have to preplan which one will be viewed first 
OR allow an option to pin a specific one to view first
OR allow an option to have the pictures in rotation
OR all of the above 
3. Link with Leio; Leio is my other one best friend! If one of my goals is to read more, it would be cool if they linked too ☺️ it has its own stats and goals menu and whatnot, but it's nice to have my habits im working on all in one place for sure! 

That's all i can think of for now! Thanks for the app💞

EDIT: oh! It would be super cool to be able to see presistency off each habit for the week days like it does on the overview, but separately☺️

Momentum is too minimalistic (though I like their desktop sync, wink!) and Strides has a bubbly interface I can’t stand. Then here comes Today: sleek, customizable, effective, and innovative.

I left feedback for a couple of things I’d like to see, but seeing their response to prior comments and where the app is now, I have no doubt they’ll continue to improve the app and likely implement what I mentioned. Over the summer before getting my Oura ring for sleep tracking, I was using Pillow by the same developers as Today (but didn’t know it), and it’s equally great. In fact I gave Oura feedback to implement some of what Pillow has! It’s like this developer and their apps popped out of nowhere, and I’m happy to have discovered them.

title: Great potential, not quite there though.
body:
I have been through every app in the app store for habit trackers - this one is my favorite because it doesn’t feel like just another to do list, calendar, or chore. It’s actually fun! It’s personal, and it’s genuinely helpful. I love it. A couple problems I run into though are:
1. I lost all my data after the app crashed when I was deleting my old cover photos. That was a real bummer and since then I’ve noticed the app doesn’t automatically back up your data like it says it does. 
2. The milestone card is not useful as is. I wish you could have recurring milestones.. and you might say whatever needs to be tracked on a  recurring basis could be done with the other cards... but the milestone card is cool because it allows you to type out words so that you can add even more personalization to your habit instead of just tracking tally marks, which I think really adds an important component to motivation. 
3. The chart card is wonderful but it really needs to show CUMULATIVE data RELATIVE to your goal, not averages. I wish the Goal could be reset as well. 
4. The counter card is really great... no complaints about that.
5. I think the meditation card is cool, but I’m a subscriber to Headspace, so it would be nice I could have that data imported. 
6. The journal card is perfect. The photo card is perfect. 
7. The interface is perfect. 

As a side note I really love that you can add as many cards as possible. 

I’ve emailed the developers about these quirks so I know they are working on some of these things already. I don’t mean to be repetitive it’s just that I literally love this app so much and I’ve been telling all my friends about it... it’s so close to perfect that it makes me kind of impatient for the next update! Thanks for creating this app!!

author: Omojazz

title: App helped me drop 60lbs at the Gym!!
body:
I’ve always struggled to build a consistent habit of working out. Last year I downloaded Today in the hopes of finding a solution that will help me visualize my goals. This has been one of the best downloads I’ve ever made. I even paid for premium pack! 

1) Easy to use interface makes it super simple to check-in your habit. If you use the widget — makes it even easier! 

2) Streak Calendar allows me to see how many days of the week I’ve been consistent. It marks the day in a green box to give you a sense of accomplishment! 

3) You can add different cards to your habit tracker. For example, there is a journal entry card I use to log which body part I’ve worked on and how much time I’ve spent in Cardio. I also use the photo card to take my progress pics! 

4) It backs up to iCloud Drive so you don’t lose your tracking data, streaks, badges, and settings. 

5) Super customizable so your goals can be changed to daily, weekly, monthly, even asking which days of the week or how many days of the week you want to check-in your habit. Also, it sends you reminders if you allow notifications. 

6) You can log multiple habits. For example, I use it to log my gym workouts, I use it to practice mindfulness, and have used it to build a habit of reading more. 

There is so much more this app offers that I can’t possibly cover in a review, but it’s definitely worth the free download and, personally, it’s worth the premium pack price too. This app helped me build a consistent habit of going to the gym 4-5 times a week and I’ve dropped 60lbs since using it!

author: PTMBL

title: Great user interface and easy to use
body:
The app interface is wonderful. But the app is missing some essential features. 
1. Viewing number of days on a monthly calendar. I don’t need fancy graph. Just want to see my days on the calendar. (This is available now. Thanks so much.)
2. Setting a habit to include every day of the week or month. I want daily checkins.  Weekly only allows 6. Why not 7? Monthly only allows 25 not 30. These restricts are prohibitive. I don’t get it. (They added a daily option will allows all the days. That works but it does not reset like the weekly option. So I have to use daily in order to have seven checking per week. 
3. I love the added cards. I chose to use the milestone card for a project. When I checked the first milestone as completed it was removed from the list. The correct action is to show a check mark. I went through the trouble to create the list so that I could see my progress. Please allow check marks instead of deleting. 
4. Streaks. I’d like to know see my streaks. Not just how many days badge. If I performed an activity 21 times but not in a row then this is not a 21 day streak. A streak is number of consecutive days. 

This app has potential. But has  many small issues. 

I purchased the pro version and I’m hoping the developers will continue to work out the problems. So far great job. This app is going to be awesome if they continue on the path their on.

Thank you for this app and your continued support.

title: ...and Apple won’t give me a refund
body:
It’s been two days with the premium version and I already hate it. 

In my attempt to stick to my routine and build goals, I must have searched for 2 hours different apps that were not only easy to use, aesthetically pretty but also showed me my progress over the long term and, most importantly, let me have multiple reminders though-out the day. Believe it or not, there are very few apps that let you have multiple check-ins. This app (I thought) fit all the criteria.

After downloading, what I thought was the starter (free) version, I soon realized I accidentally bought the premium (oops) but decided to try it out. After putting all my routines and goals in, complete with reminders. I waited for the first bell to remind me. Nothing. Thinking, maybe I forget to check and save my reminder option, I went back - nope, everything checked and save. I waited for the next reminder. Nothing. I deleted everything and started over, making sure everything was checked and saved. Still nothing. 

As a someone who needs an extra push sometimes, even in the form of a bell or simple pop-up message on my phone, this app is useless. All pretty pictures and no value. 

However, this experience did cement three things in me (things that, for whatever reason, I didn’t listen to earlier) and teach me another: 
 1. Apple (post Steve Jobs) has terrible customer service. They make you wait two days just to tell you no. Steve Jobs would have given me a refund. 
2. If you need reminders, don’t bother with apps, just use the pre-set alarm function in your phone (on iPhone, it’s under Clock) or watch. You’ve already bought it & it’s more dependable. 
3. If you want to keep track of routines & habits, don’t rely on an app to do your work for you. Either set up an Excel spreadsheet that lists the date, time, & activity. You can then sort and chart your progress easily after a set period of time. P.S. you can also set alarms in Excel. Don’t like Excel, Google “Bullet Journal” on how to keep a routine & habit tracker. 
4. Pay attention to what you are doing, you’ll never get that time back.

title: Gorgeous but ...
body:
There is a lot to love about this app but it is missing a few key functions that make habit tracking more successful. In addition to “check ins” (positive score) there ought to be a way to record “missed check -ins” (negative score) and just also a way to log days where you missed your habit but it was intentional (neutral/no penalty score). The metrics of only seeing your number of check ins is a useless metric without also seeing those days you dropped the ball. 

It’s also be great to see two habits side by side so you can see if your “early to bed” habit has a correlation to “deep work” the following day—another reason why showing “missed” days would be useful. 

I like how you can schedule a habit that has a once/week (or whatever) frequency but I’d love to see a countdown on that habit so you know, “3 more days left in week to accomplish habit”

The ability to add in widgets is amazing! Design is beautiful ... Just wish some of the basic habit-tracking functionality was more useful.

The app also features the ability to determine how many times per day, week or month the task should be done as well as custom reminders for individual tasks.

title: Honest Feedback for the Devs
body:
This app has a lot of potential. I tried a wide variety of daily habit apps and this was, by far, the most beautiful and intuitive. A couple suggestions to help make it even better:

1) The swiping between "cards" makes sense and the animation looks nice, but there's a noticeable delay that makes it feel a little clunky. It's as if each card needs to load after swipe and doesn't allow me to quickly swipe between tasks; I have to wait a second or two with every swipe. This might seem insignificant but it's really a nuisance once you have more than a handful of tasks.

2) I don't fully understand the "Today's Covers". They seem to not update and the selection is rather limited. These photos look like they come from free CC0 sources, like Unsplash, so why not add a larger selection?

3) This more a nice-to-have idea but it would be great if Fitbit data could also be synced with the health graph.

Please keep up the good work, this really is a useful app that is nearly perfect.

title: Watch App Doesn't Work
body: I use only the Watch app, as I need to track things while I am active.   The watch app, though promising, does not work well enough to rely upon.   First, it is sluggish.  It is unclear why you need to use the "Sync To Phone" force-touch item.  Is this a requirement?  Won't it sync automatically?   If you click it, will it replace your watch with the phone's tracking values?  No feedback when you do it.  Second, when you "check in", there is a long period, sometimes 15 seconds, before you get any feedback that your "check in" has completed.   The worst part is that often I go back later in the day only to find out that several "check ins" I did earlier had reverted to "not done".  This has now happened for enough days that I find the watch app to be mostly useless and unreliable.  Great idea.  In fact, I bought the premium because it has all the features I need.  It just doesn't deliver because of implementation flaws.

title: Light years ahead of other habit trackers--get Premium!
body:
This is the most beautiful app currently on my phone. The functionality matches the looks. The ability to add counters, totals, milestones and other metrics to a habit makes this the most powerful habit app out there. You can see the data behind your habits. I love that I can add covers to the habits, I've added related artwork that subtly reminds me why I'm doing the habit in the first place. 

One reviewer said that since each habit has it's own page, it makes marking off many habits difficult. That makes no sense to me. The main page has a complete list of all Habits and you can mark off basic habit completions off from there as you would in other habit apps. The beauty behind this app is you can really dive deep into your specific habit and keep track of important progress/data. 

For example, I have a sales goal to contact 50 prospects per day. I can use a resettable counter to count each time I make a contact. I can use the custom chart to track my daily total. And I can use another counter to keep track of my totals for the year. And I can use milestones to keep track of long-term goals (e.g. 1000 contacts). 

The only thing I'd add would be the ability to export everything to CSV so I can also look at the data on Google Sheets. Also a Slack integration and desktop app would get me really excited... :)

At the core of it, you can create different habits, set reminders for them, add milestones and track progression.

But what makes this app truly powerful is, the ability to add a bunch of "cards" in a dashboard type fashion. EVERYTHING that is in your Apple Healthkit can be displayed and values for can be entered. 
It can read and write every information in the healthkit and display them in every combination you want. Brilliant!

I tried all popular health dashboards and activity tracker, but this is miles ahead of anything else. 
Also, the design is excellent. It looks sleek and the functionality is super smooth.

Really glad I found this app!

title: Great app, great pricing model
body:
First and foremost this is a great app for allowing you to hold yourself accountable and create new habits or squash old ones. It does exactly what it says it does and does so in a very easy to use and overall "pretty" interface. 

I love that I suggested a feature I would like to see and received a timely, personal response from the development team. 

Lastly, I love the, what I'm calling, "payment model" this company is using. The app is free to download with an available in-app purchase. The free app allows you to add a habit and try it out fully for that one habit. Then if you like it, pay $4.99 (well worth it) to unlock unlimited habits as well as other niceties like Touch ID support to lock the app down and backup via the cloud. I know this model doesn't work for every developer or app but it certainly is perfection here. 

Highly recommend this if you want a simple way to keep track of habits and are trying to make positive change in your life.

title: It's an investment. No matter the price.

To maintain these stepping stones to success you need simplicity, the ease of simply knowing you did the right thing and you've come ever further on your journey. But you also want to option for complexity. The knowledge of how you've gotten there. Of how far you've come.

This app gives you that option. The cost may seem high but the reward is ever higher. Other apps charge you for instant gratification. For amusement. This app provides you with the tools to become a better, happier, more successful person.

It cost nothing. You won't regret it if you're truly determined.

title: A happy lifestyle is worth $5
body:
I understand that people are upset about the limited functionality and forced paid version for $5. On one hand, I agree that it should have been a paid app from the start, or at least allow 2-3 habits. 

But who cares. $5, in the grand scheme of things, is nothing. That's one cup of coffee. And to anyone using an Apple product to download the app, they already forked out $600+ for the hardware,  which is substantial. The stigma here is that the App Store is so utterly saturated with free/freemium apps that I think a lot of times we forget the amount of work that goes into development... And that its intended to provide developers with an income. 

The app can be improved, and I'm sure that it will. But the $5 investment is worth every penny and more if the app gets you to do what it's intended to. The return on investment in sheer productivity or your quality of life is phenomenal if you consider that this app can help you make, and keep, good habits. And if even ONE of my current habits sticks (Floss, Meditate, Read, Run, Bodyweight Exercise), the effect it will have on my life will be much more than $5.

title: Impressively Professional, and surprisingly strong feature list, *especially for a 1.0*
body:

I've often wished for a habit-tracking app that would somehow give you a reward for achieving your goals... I really can't think of S business model for it, though. Perhaps coupons or digital rewards... I'd be extra motivated to complete my daily goals if doing them earned me something like: 
•a coupon for discounted goodies, like Starbucks maybe.
•small amounts of "coins" or other game currency in fun iOS games (maybe you could partner with someone)
Both of those options could be good for the other businesses involved. If the game has ads, at least. Now, these should be strictly the users' choice: I don't want game currency for games I don't play or coupons for businesses I do not visit. 
It could be a sort of menu... You get points for your goals and you choose what to redeem them for...

(obviously it has to be an honor-system thing, at least non-exercise goals, and even then you can manually change health app data)

title: AMAZING APP! But…
body:
I love this app. It makes tracking habits easy and enjoyable.

But it has 2 serious problems:

(Update: both of the following problems are reported by the developer to be resolved in a future update - the developer feed back is great)

1. Why can't I check off a habit that is NOT a daily habit multiple times in a day? If I have a habit 6 days a week, and then I miss a day, I'd like to be able to check off that habit twice the next day in order to make up for missing the previous day! And why is the number of check-ins fixed? Why can't I check-in a 7th time if I happen to do a 6 day habit more than 6 times in a week?

2. Bugs. Swiping from side to side feels great but doesn't work very well. When I swipe horizontally, I have have to wait a second before I can swipe again otherwise the app won't recognize the second swipe. The app also frequently recognizes horizontal swipes as vertical swipes. And finally not being able to swipe horizontally when viewing the cards of a habit is extremely frustrating.

body: Nice, helpful app, just a bit one-dimensional, needs something more to add to the app. I forget to use it as it does such a small task, maybe add a new idea and dimension to the app.
author: Perks ;)

title: Really great intuitive app...
body: I use this app daily to track my habits - it's simple to use and easy to track. 3D Touch support makes it a simple matter of pressing the screen to mark habits as complete. Habits are easy to add and switch between too. If you forget to mark a day, simply swipe up to mark it on the calendar. Adding cards to your habit allows you to create custom milestones and see stats for your habits as well.
author: GavinBooyens

title: "Toady loves your Dukiness"
body:
"Do you like using Toady?" Flashed up on my screen and reminded me of Gummi Bears. 
Yes, I like it. It actually does help me develop habits. Everyday I practice guitar,  writing, get a minimum core done for work by minimising interruptions, get to the gym, smoke less, be nice to those I love and feel like I've achieved something at the end of a week, like I'm getting somewhere, like the rat race is less rat and more a journey of development.
